messages.subject: Centering variables in random slopes
parts:
Hi,

I am fitting a simple model to some count data, analyzing fixed effects of time. I have time series data for multiple groups so I have included a group random intercept and slope. I was playing around with the effects of centering (or standardizing) my time covariate and surprised to find some differences in my fixed effects of time. This only occurs when I have random time slopes. It is not major but I am not sure which one to go with.

Any advice would be much appreciated:

model1<-inla(Count~time+f(Group.int,model="iid")+f(Group.idx,time,model="iid"),data=inla_df,family="poisson")

On Mon, 2015-08-17 at 00:25 -0700, SpNine wrote:

> I am fitting a simple model to some count data, analyzing fixed
> effects of time. I have time series data for multiple groups so I
> have included a group random intercept and slope. I was playing
> around with the effects of centering (or standardizing) my time
> covariate and surprised to find some differences in my fixed effects
> of time. This only occurs when I have random time slopes. It is not
> major but I am not sure which one to go with.

Hi

if you run with uncentered 'time' and centered 'time', you implicitely
change the (joint) prior for the slope and intercept. this is why the
results change.
